headline: Everything in this niche
body: Estrogen, androgens, growth hormone, IGF-1. That's the entire framework people use to think about height.
punch: A stimulant sits completely outside that framework and still shows up.

headline: Methylphenidate
body: Applied to growth plate tissue in vitro, it promoted premature growth plate closure — the same endpoint estrogen drives, reached by a completely different route.
punch: A non-hormonal drug hitting a hormonal endpoint.

headline: Then the clinical data
body: Children and adolescents on central stimulants for up to 16 years showed reduced body weight and a temporary halt in growth, with implications for final stature.
punch: This is one of the larger longitudinal datasets in the whole topic.

headline: Note the word
body: A halt is not the same as depletion. Growth suppression that slows the division rate can conserve proliferative capacity — which is the mechanism behind catch-up growth.
punch: Suppressed and spent are different outcomes with different endings.

headline: So what's the honest read
body: A real signal worth knowing about, from two independent directions. Not a settled quantified effect on adult height, and the in vitro dose may not reflect real prescribing.

headline: Do not stop
body: Untreated ADHD carries substantial documented harm — academic, social, and injury risk. Nothing here outweighs that, and none of it is individual medical advice.
punch: If this concerns you the move is a conversation with the prescriber. Nothing else.

headline: Why this matters anyway
body: It shows the growth plate responds to drug classes nobody thought to check. The hormone-only framework this entire niche runs on is incomplete.
punch: The interesting question is what else has never been looked at.

headline: It's never over
body: Real mechanisms, real citations, no protocols.
